profile.reading:
Per Flexential's own individual facility page, this building (Flexential Louisville - Downtown) is located at 752 Barret Avenue, Louisville, KY 40204. The operator publishes a footprint of 61080 square feet and 3.09 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building, with published certifications and compliance attestations including PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, HITRUST, ISO 27001, SSAE 18. Kentucky utility LG&E and KU reported in May 2026 that as many as 30 data center projects were under discussion statewide, with 11 having at least a 50% probability of proceeding and requiring roughly 3.5 gigawatts of electricity, enough to power more than 2 million homes; the parent company's CEO said total prospective demand could reach around 12 gigawatts, against Kentucky's maximum generation capacity of 18.4 gigawatts as of summer 2024, per Kentucky Lantern's reporting. LG&E and KU identified four data center projects as "imminent," at roughly 80% probability, including a planned development in West Louisville. Kentucky lawmakers have offered sales-tax incentives for data centers but had not, as of 2026, enacted regulatory protections requiring the facilities to fund their own dedicated infrastructure; a GOP-backed bill to require that funding failed during the 2026 legislative session.

Separate from Flexential's existing colocation footprint, Louisville is set to host Kentucky's first hyperscale data center campus, a 153-acre, seven-building project on Camp Ground Road near Shively developed by PowerHouse Data Centers and Poe Companies, described as a several-billion-dollar investment; power demand is projected to reach 400 megawatts, with an initial 130 MW targeted by October 2026 and LG&E building a dedicated switch station for the project. Louisville's Planning Commission approved the project 6-1 in March 2026 over objections from more than 20 residents who cited pollution and grid-strain concerns in the historically industrial Rubbertown-adjacent area; because current code classifies large data centers as a "telecommunications hotel" use, the project did not require Metro Council rezoning approval. In response, Louisville Metro has drafted a size-tiered data center zoning ordinance limiting facilities to 500,000 square feet, requiring conditional-use permits and setbacks of 200 to 500 feet from homes, schools, and hospitals for mid-size and large facilities, and banning co-located gas turbines; the draft drew more than 3,600 public comments ahead of a Planning Commission vote scheduled for September 3, 2026.

reading.body:
Flexential Louisville – Downtown publishes 3.09 MW of IT capacity across 61,080 square feet of technical space, positioning it for regulated enterprise workloads rather than frontier AI training.

The facility holds seven compliance certifications spanning financial controls, healthcare data, payment processing, and information security frameworks. SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II address operational controls for audited environments. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment-card systems. HITRUST qualifies it for healthcare information. ISO 27001 establishes a recognized security management standard. SSAE 18 is the auditing standard under which SOC reports are issued. This certification stack targets enterprises and regulated industries, not hyperscale training clusters.

At 3.09 MW, this campus ranks second among three Kentucky facilities publishing capacity figures, representing roughly 32 percent of the state's published total of 9.55 MW. The power envelope supports approximately 309 racks at 10 kW per rack, or 77 racks at 40 kW per rack, though Flexential has not published a per-rack ceiling for this specific facility. At current scale, this campus falls below the threshold where frontier-model training clusters are typically built today, though it may support inference, enterprise AI applications, or regulated data processing workloads.
